metadata.title: Domestic Freight Corridor Flow Density
metadata.section: Section F: Logistics, Infrastructure & Public Health
metadata.data_notes: Per-highway freight tonnage is not published monthly. National freight volume measures are shown instead.

events.label: COVID: rail carloads hit a record low
Record 1.28 million rail containers in a month

explanation.summary: How much freight moves across the country by truck and rail each month. Freight falls early in recessions and recovers with spending on goods. Rail has two very different businesses: bulk carloads (coal, grain, chemicals) are shrinking, while containers (intermodal) are growing.
explanation.methodology: Freight Transportation Services Index (BTS), truck tonnage index (American Trucking Associations), rail carloads and rail intermodal units (Association of American Railroads), all monthly and seasonally adjusted, via FRED. Tonnage by individual highway is not published monthly, so national measures are shown instead.

key_findings.title: 2009: Freight Recession
key_findings.description: Truck tonnage fell 13% from mid-2008 to April 2009. The freight index hit 94.9, its lowest on the chart.
key_findings.significance: Freight is one of the first parts of the economy to fall.

key_findings.title: 2019: The Freight Peak
key_findings.description: The freight index reached 141 and truck tonnage 120, both the highest on the chart, before trade disputes slowed shipments.
key_findings.significance: Freight peaked months before the pandemic.

key_findings.title: 2021: Containers at a Record
key_findings.description: Rail intermodal reached a record 1.28 million units in a month as imported goods poured in. Rail carloads, hit by falling coal shipments, are 28% below their 2007 peak.
key_findings.significance: Rail has shifted from hauling coal to hauling containers.
